pieces.h: Exam Details
pieces.t: Mississippi does not use one single statewide journeyman electrician exam for every individual electrician. Journeyman electrician licensing, registration, and testing requirements are commonly set by local jurisdictions. A candidate may need to follow the rules of a city, county, municipal licensing board, local building department, or other local authority. A commonly used journeyman-level electrical exam format is the ICC National Standard Journeyman Electrician exam. That exam includes 80 multiple-choice questions, allows 4 hours of testing time, and is open book. Its subject areas include general knowledge, services and service equipment, feeders, branch circuits and conductors, wiring methods and materials, equipment and devices, control devices, motors and generators, and special occupancies, equipment, and conditions. The ICC National Standard Journeyman Electrician exam places strong emphasis on wiring methods and materials, branch circuits and conductors, equipment and devices, services and service equipment, and special occupancies, equipment, and conditions.

pieces.h: Exam Details
pieces.t: These are practical journeyman-level areas that require candidates to understand both NEC rules and field application. Some Mississippi cities or counties may use different approved exams, local applications, separate passing scores, local code amendments, different testing providers, or specific experience documentation. Candidates preparing for a Mississippi journeyman electrician credential should match their study materials to the exam required by the jurisdiction where they are applying. This Ultimate Combo is focused on 2026 NEC-based journeyman electrician exam preparation. It helps candidates prepare for code-based testing, calculation questions, trade knowledge review, and timed exam-style practice using a complete set of study tools.

pieces.h: Open Book Test
pieces.t: The ICC National Standard Journeyman Electrician exam is an open book test. Candidates taking that exam may use approved reference materials during the examination, subject to the exam provider’s rules. Because Mississippi journeyman electrician testing is commonly controlled at the local level, candidates must follow the exam-room rules for the specific exam they are scheduled to take. Open book testing still requires strong preparation. The National Electrical Code is a detailed technical reference, and a candidate who is unfamiliar with its structure can lose valuable time searching through unrelated articles. A prepared candidate should be able to identify the subject of the question, locate the correct NEC article or table, interpret the wording, and apply the rule accurately. The included National Electrical Code 2026 Paperback with Tabs is intended to help candidates practice code navigation before exam day.

pieces.t: During study sessions, candidates can use the tabbed NEC to become familiar with definitions, general requirements, wiring and protection, wiring methods and materials, equipment for general use, special occupancies, special equipment, special conditions, communications systems, tables, and calculation-related provisions. Open book does not mean every answer is easy to find. Some questions may require electrical theory, practical trade knowledge, calculation skills, or the ability to compare code sections. Other questions may require candidates to use table notes, understand exceptions, or apply a rule to a specific installation condition. Timed practice helps candidates build the speed and confidence needed for this type of exam. The NEC included in this package is for study and code-navigation preparation. Exam-room use depends on the approved reference rules issued by the exam provider or local Mississippi authority.

pieces.h: Licensing Steps
pieces.t: Mississippi journeyman electrician licensing steps depend on the local authority that issues or recognizes the credential. A candidate may need to apply through a city licensing office, county department, municipal board, local building department, or electrical licensing authority. Since Mississippi does not issue one uniform statewide individual journeyman electrician license, identifying the correct local jurisdiction is the first step. A typical Mississippi journeyman electrician path may include completing supervised electrical work experience, finishing apprenticeship or classroom training when required, gathering employer verification, submitting a local application, paying required local fees, scheduling the approved electrical examination, passing the required exam, and completing any remaining local licensing or registration steps.

pieces.h: Licensing Steps
pieces.t: Local requirements may include a minimum number of years or hours of electrical experience, proof of work under a licensed electrician or electrical contractor, apprenticeship completion, classroom instruction, identification documents, continuing education, or a local sponsor. Some jurisdictions may recognize an exam passed through a national provider, while others may require a specific local exam or local review process. Mississippi electrical contractor licensing is separate from local journeyman-level credentialing. Commercial and residential contractors are licensed through the Mississippi State Board of Contractors when the work falls within state contractor licensing requirements. A journeyman credential generally supports trade-level work and employment, while contracting authority requires the proper contractor licensing, business structure, and regulatory approval.

pieces.h: State Requirements
pieces.t: Mississippi does not have one statewide individual journeyman electrician license issued to every electrician. Individual journeyman electrician requirements are commonly handled locally by cities, counties, and municipalities. Candidates should prepare for the rules of the jurisdiction where the credential is needed. One local authority may require a journeyman electrician exam and documented field experience, while another may recognize a national journeyman-level exam or focus on contractor registration. Some employers may also require a journeyman-level credential as part of hiring, promotion, or jobsite qualification standards. Common preparation areas for Mississippi journeyman electrician candidates include National Electrical Code knowledge, electrical theory, services, feeders, branch circuits, conductors, wiring methods, raceways, boxes, grounding and bonding, overcurrent protection, motors, control devices, equipment, special occupancies, special equipment, safety, and electrical calculations.

pieces.h: State Requirements

A journeyman credential generally supports trade-level recognition and employment. Electrical contracting may require separate contractor licensing, registration, insurance, business authorization, permit privileges, or proof of a qualifying party, depending on the work and jurisdiction involved. pieces.t: NEC tabs help candidates locate major articles, chapters, tables, and subject areas faster during study. This supports stronger code-navigation practice and helps candidates become more comfortable using the NEC as a reference.

pieces.h: Q: Does this package include calculation practice?
pieces.t: Yes. The 2026 Electrician Calculations Study Guide is included to help candidates review calculation topics that commonly appear on master electrician exams.

pieces.h: Q: Does a local Mississippi master electrician credential automatically allow statewide electrical contracting?
pieces.t: No. Local individual credentials and state contractor licensing are separate considerations. Candidates who plan to contract for electrical work should review Mississippi State Board of Contractors requirements and any local requirements that apply.

pieces.h: Q: Does this package guarantee that I will pass?
pieces.t: No. This package is designed to support preparation through organized study materials, code review, calculations practice, flash cards, online questions, and structured study guidance. Exam results depend on the candidate’s preparation, knowledge, and performance.

pieces.h: Q: Should I confirm Mississippi licensing requirements before testing?
pieces.t: Yes. Candidates should confirm the required license classification, local jurisdiction rules, state contractor requirements, application process, code edition, reference rules, and post-exam licensing steps before scheduling or taking an exam.

pieces.h: Q: Is this combo based on the 2026 NEC?
pieces.t: Yes. This combo is based on the 2026 National Electrical Code and includes the National Electrical Code 2026 Paperback.

pieces.h: Q: What books are included in this package?
pieces.t: This package includes the 2026 Mississippi Master Electrician Study Guide, the 2026 Electrician Calculations Study Guide, and the National Electrical Code 2026 Paperback.

pieces.h: Q: Who should use this Mississippi master electrician combo?
pieces.t: This combo is intended for electricians preparing for Mississippi master electrician or electrical contractor exam content, NEC-based questions, open-book code navigation, and electrical calculation problems.

pieces.h: Q: Does Mississippi have state electrical contractor licensing?
pieces.t: Yes. The Mississippi State Board of Contractors regulates state contractor licensing, including electrical contractor work that falls under state licensing requirements.

pieces.h: Q: Are local Mississippi electrical requirements still important?
pieces.t: Yes. Local jurisdictions may have their own master electrician, permit, registration, inspection, or licensing requirements. Candidates should review the rules for the city, county, or municipality where they plan to work.

pieces.h: Q: Does this package help with electrical calculations?
pieces.t: Yes. The 2026 Electrician Calculations Study Guide is included to help candidates practice formulas, NEC table use, load calculations, conductor sizing, raceway fill, box fill, service calculations, and other calculation-based topics.

pieces.h: Q: Can I study directly from the NEC with this package?
pieces.t: Yes. The National Electrical Code 2026 Paperback is included so candidates can study article language, definitions, tables, exceptions, and code requirements directly.

pieces.h: Q: Does this package replace the official licensing application?
pieces.t: No. This package is for exam preparation. Candidates must still follow the application, testing, and licensing instructions from the Mississippi State Board of Contractors or the applicable local authority.

pieces.h: Exam Room Approved Books
pieces.t:
National Electrical Code
The NEC is the primary code reference commonly used for Mississippi electrical contractor and local master electrician exams. Candidates should use the NEC edition approved for their scheduled exam.
Mississippi Law and Business Management Reference Materials
Business and law reference materials may be required for Mississippi contractor licensing exams when the applicant must pass the Law and Business Management examination.

pieces.h: Q: Who is this Mississippi Master Electrician exam prep combo for?
pieces.t: This combo is for electricians preparing for the Mississippi Master Electrician exam who want a study guide, flash cards, 12 practice exams, and 2 full final exams in one structured preparation package.

pieces.h: Q: Is this product based on the 2026 National Electrical Code?
pieces.t: Yes. This product is based on the 2026 National Electrical Code and is designed to support NEC-focused electrical exam preparation.

pieces.h: Q: Does this product include practice exams?
pieces.t: Yes. This package includes 12 practice exams plus 2 full final exams. The practice exams help you build familiarity with exam-style questions, while the final exams help you evaluate readiness after completing more of your study plan.

pieces.h: Q: Are flash cards included?
pieces.t: Yes. This is a study guide and flash card combo. The flash cards are designed to help reinforce electrical terms, formulas, definitions, NEC concepts, safety topics, calculations, and exam-style recall.

pieces.h: Q: Is the Mississippi Master Electrician exam open book?
pieces.t: Yes. The Mississippi Master Electrician exam is an open book test. Candidates are responsible for bringing their own approved references to the examination center.

pieces.h: Q: How many questions are on the MSBOC Master Electrician exam?
pieces.t: The MSBOC Master Electrician state-specific exam contains 80 questions.

pieces.h: Q: How much time is allowed for the Mississippi Master Electrician exam?
pieces.t: The MSBOC Master Electrician state-specific exam allows 3 hours for completion.

pieces.h: Q: What is the passing score for the Mississippi Master Electrician exam?
pieces.t: The passing score for the MSBOC Master Electrician state-specific exam is 70%.

pieces.h: Q: What references are allowed in the Mississippi Master Electrician exam room?
pieces.t: The approved references include the National Electrical Code, Code of Federal Regulations - 29 CFR Part 1926 or the PSI selections version, and Ugly’s Electrical References by George V. Hart.

pieces.h: Q: Does Mississippi require a Business and Law exam?
pieces.t: Yes. Mississippi requires the Law and Business Management exam for all contractor applicants. A trade exam may also be required based on the license classification being requested.

pieces.h: Q: Does this combo guarantee that I will pass the exam?
pieces.t: No. This product is designed to support preparation through structured study, practice exams, final exams, flash card review, reference navigation, and NEC-based preparation. Exam results and licensing approval depend on the candidate’s preparation, testing performance, and Mississippi licensing requirements.
